title: FastPass: Incident-to-Roadmap Escalation Flow for Critical Accounts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Strategic customers occasionally surface urgent operational or feature blockers via support/CS that warrant accelerated product commitments. Current intake is ad-hoc, causing missed SLAs and misaligned expectations. The FastPass flow is a structured, timeboxed pathway from a critical account incident to a defensible roadmap commitment or an explicit compensating action.
objectives: Define a 5-step FastPass workflow (Triage -> Impact Assessment -> Commitment Decision -> Scoped Delivery Plan -> Closure)
Create deterministic decision criteria for when an incident qualifies for FastPass (signals + thresholds)
Ship a lightweight triage form + Slack escalation channel + runbook for SRE/CS/AE/PM handoff
Integrate FastPass tickets with roadmap lanes and create automatic visibility in Console for affected routes/models
Measure time-to-decision and adherence to commitment windows; target 90% decision within 10 business days
acceptance_criteria: A documented qualification matrix that maps account tier, incident severity, and business impact to FastPass eligibility
A templated FastPass PRD + scoped delivery checklist that can convert a decision into a release plan within 3 days
A Slack escalation channel and a triage Google Form that captures the minimum required fields for engineering evaluation
Dashboard in Console that surfaces active FastPasses, SLA windows, and owner(s)
Pilot with two enterprise customers and one dedicated CSM to validate the flow and gather feedback
success_metrics: % FastPass decisions completed within 10 business days >= 90%
% FastPass commitments that meet scoped delivery windows >= 80%
Reduction in ad-hoc executive escalations related to roadmap commitments by 60%
NPS delta for pilot accounts +5 attributable to clarity of escalation outcomes
stakeholders: Legal: Claire Benson (review for contractual implications)
operational_runbook: Step 0: Customer files incident with tag 'fastpass-candidate' or CS flags in triage form
Step 1: PM + SRE perform 48h initial impact assessment and mark eligibility
Step 2: If eligible, PM convenes FastPass guild (PM/Eng/SRE/CS/AE) to produce a decision within 10 business days
Step 3: Decision outcomes: Commit (scoped feature + timeline), Defer (clear rationale + compensating actions), or Escalate to Exec (when cross-org tradeoffs required)
Step 4: Create a FastPass ticket in Linear with release and owner tags; surface in Console fastpass dashboard
Step 5: Close FastPass with postmortem + customer communication templates and lessons learned capture
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: FastPass becomes a backdoor to bypass prioritization -> Mitigation: Eligibility matrix and quarterly audit of FastPass-to-release conversions
Risk: Engineering capacity churn on short notice -> Mitigation: Dedicated contingency buffer in Dedicated pools or bump policy to use fallback models + opt-in burst capacity
Risk: Legal/contract exposure for implied commitments -> Mitigation: template language for commitments, Legal sign-off required when commitment > 60 business days
open_questions: Should FastPass decisions automatically reserve Dedicated capacity or request burst only on approval?
What SLAs should be contractually offered vs. operational goals? (Legal input required)
How do we weight FastPass commits against quarterly OKRs without derailing key initiatives?
Which Console permissions are required to view FastPass tickets and customer-sensitive data in the dashboard?
